name: Jeriah
overview: Jeriah was a male Levite, specifically a descendant of Hebron, belonging to the Hebronites who came from Kohath, son of Levi. He held a leadership position as chief among the Hebronites from Jazer of Gilead. His tribal affiliation and role highlight his importance within the Levitical structure during his time.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeriah, also rendered Jerijah, means 'YHWH founds,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's foundational role. This proper name is not recorded as being given directly by God but carries significant meaning related to divine establishment.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Jeriah as a descendant of Hebron, establishing his lineage within the Hebronites. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are documented in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Jeriah's significance lies in his leadership among the Hebronites, a Levitical clan descended from Kohath. As chief from Jazer of Gilead, he represents the organizational and tribal divisions of the Levites, which were crucial for temple service and religious duties. His mention underscores the detailed genealogical and tribal records preserved in Scripture to maintain the order of worship and community identity.
